decisions.rationale: Accepted on the critic's interim remedy, under the captain's direction (2026-11-09) not to split reporting-indexes-and-review, which spans F22 to F24. Verified: (1) the stale note is fixed: reporting-indexes-and-review/module.json no longer says the project brief teaches JDBC concepts 'no earlier page covers' and now names the F23 bridge pages as where they are first taught; jdbc-data-access-project/topic.json's html absence reason is updated the same way. (2) The calendar inversion is recorded with its rationale in jdbc-data-access/module.json (Module placement note: moduleOrder is structural grouping, not a reordering of calendar days) and in module-plan.md (Acceptance: Course order). (3) Delivered order is bound by curriculum, not moduleOrder: all five jdbc-data-access topics carry curriculum pointer /tracks/0/weeks/4/days/2 with calendarDayIds F23; subqueries-and-ctes, window-functions-top-n-per-group, indexes and query-plans-with-explain carry /days/1 (F22); sql-review-joins-grouping-window-functions and jdbc-review carry /days/3 (F24); the repo tooling uses moduleOrder only for lock/tree enumeration and T14 budgets per calendar day. course.json is unchanged (sha 64570fa5...). Residual, not blocking: intake.md's 'modules follow calendar day order' rule text is not amended, and this module branch edits reporting-indexes-and-review catalog files outside its own module scope per the delivery rule; both are captain-directed and should be noted at merge.
